title: Understanding and origination come apart
explanation: The account adds distinctions to the question of what counts as the writer's own thinking, but expressly says the human–AI comparison remains unanswered. This records conceptual elaboration, not an established change in learning.

title: An acknowledgment does not finish the repair
explanation: The repair concerns the comparison and its assumptions, not a settled verdict on permission. The published account explicitly moves from asking where a boundary is drawn to questioning whether feedback and idea generation can be separated in that way. Acknowledgment is followed by recurrence, so the repair cannot be counted as a single uncomplicated success.

title: Hardwig qualifies the demand for self-sufficiency
explanation: The article explicitly states that the later reading qualifies an emerging emphasis on explaining and defending everything. It does not record a completed before-and-after demonstration of the writer's theological competence or a definite change in the overarching conclusion.

title: The writer becomes a reader of preserved work
explanation: The later formulation distinguishes the evidence required for learning from the evidence required for contribution. The source asks what can be explained at different times; it does not supply the paired performance evidence needed to establish an individual learning gain.

title: A theological inference is tested in a hypothetical case
explanation: These are contrasting possible applications, explicitly presented as proposed tests rather than observations from a completed study. No learner is recorded moving from the mistaken inference to the alternative.

title: ICAP qualifies what conversation alone can show
explanation: The paragraph explicitly reports a qualification of what can be inferred from conversational format. No earlier coded passage establishes that the writer had asserted that all chatbot dialogue proves learning, so an earlier claim is left unassigned.
